textRuns.value: WHAT IS WRONG WITH THE LEFT-HAND SIDE OF THESE CHARTS
Cheap films look extraordinary here, and they are partly an illusion. Revenue reporting is not random: it depends on how big the film was.
Of films budgeted between $10,000 and $100,000, only 7.8% report any revenue at all. Of films budgeted above $50M, 91.1% do.

A cheap film that flopped usually never had its revenue recorded, so it is absent from every chart on this page. An expensive flop is recorded and counted. That means the return of the cheapest band is an upper bound on reality, not an expectation — and it is why this report does not advise anyone to make cheap films.
Only 2.4% of films in the $10,000-$100,000 band survive into this analysis, against 90.8% of films above $50M.
